edges.reason: msg.sender is the recipient of the refund low-level call, so it can re-enter changeToColor while it is still executing.
msg.sender is checked against ownerOf(index[_index]) to authorize each color conversion.
msg.sender receives the excess ETH refund low-level call in mintNFT, allowing re-entrant minting.
msg.sender is the mint recipient inside mintNFT.
msg.sender must equal _owner and is the destination of the full balance transfer.
The constructor assigns msg.sender to _owner, making the deployer privileged.
The owner identity derived from msg.sender gates setReadyForSale.
approve requires msg.sender to be the token owner or an approved operator.
transferFrom requires msg.sender to be approved or the owner.
safeTransferFrom authorizes the caller using msg.sender.
safeTransferFrom with data authorizes the caller using msg.sender.
setApprovalForAll stores approvals under msg.sender and rejects operator == msg.sender.
msg.sender is passed as the operator argument into the untrusted onERC721Received callback.
changeToColor performs the refund external call after partial state updates, exposing re-entrancy.
changeToColor calls _safeMint which can invoke an external receiver callback mid-loop.
changeToColor burns the original bw token before minting its color counterpart.
changeToColor queries the price curve with distributionCurve(true).
changeToColor computes colorIndex with the SafeMath addition.
The addition result is stored in colorIndex and used as the new token id.
changeToColor decrements the refundable amount with SafeMath.sub.
The calldata index element is the base of the computed color token id.
The residual returnAmount determines the value sent in the untrusted refund call.
mintNFT performs an external refund call using the residual msg.value.
mintNFT derives the mint index from blockhash, a manipulable entropy source.
mintNFT mints via _safeMint, invoking the receiver callback inside the while loop.
mintNFT subtracts the mint price from the remaining value each iteration.
The subtraction result is written back into returnAmount.
availableNFTs.length bounds the blockhash-derived random index.
The chosen random index is used to record the price paid in mintedPrice.
The random index selects and removes an entry from availableNFTs.
Each successful mint increments mintedCounter.
Each successful color conversion increments colorCounter.
mintedCounter selects the bw price tier in the distribution curve.
colorCounter selects the color price tier in the distribution curve.
_forColor switches the curve between color and bw counters.
_counter drives every price branch in distributionCurve.
weiAmount is the returned price value of the curve.
distributionCurve(true) supplies requiredWei in changeToColor.
requiredWei gates the loop progress and refund accounting in changeToColor.
distributionCurve(false) supplies mintPrice controlling the mint loop.
withdraw gates the balance transfer behind msg.sender == _owner.
The cached balance is the amount sent by the owner-only transfer.

normalization_plan.reason: The _forColor parameter only selects a branch of the distributionCurve price function and carries no independent semantics.
The _counter local is a transient copy of the mint/color counters used solely inside distributionCurve.
The weiAmount local is the return value of distributionCurve and is fully absorbed by that function.
The calldata index array is consumed only by changeToColor for iteration, ownership checks and color id derivation.
returnAmount exists only to size the ETH value sent by the untrusted refund call in changeToColor.
requiredWei is the per-iteration price used exclusively inside the changeToColor loop.
colorIndex is a temporary mint argument produced and consumed entirely inside changeToColor.
mintPrice is the loop condition and payment amount used only inside mintNFT.
returnAmount in mintNFT is a running refund accumulator consumed by that function only.
randomMintIndex is a transient loop variable selecting entries of availableNFTs in mintNFT.
The balance local is cached only to be transferred by the owner-only withdraw function.
